title: Anchoring Enterprise GenAI with Knowledge Graphs: Jonathan Lowe (Pfizer), Stephen Chin (Neo4j)
talk_summary: A Pfizer data scientist and Neo4j's Stephen Chin describe building a production GraphRAG system over millions of manufacturing technology-transfer documents, chunking documents into a knowledge graph to improve retrieval precision and explainability. Most of the talk is organizational navigation advice (selling to executives, client partners, vendors), with a smaller technical core about graph-structured chunking and hybrid vector+graph retrieval.

takeaways.technique: Graph-structured chunking with hybrid vector+graph retrieval
takeaways.what_they_do: They store document chunks as nodes in a graph with explicit structure (document/block/paragraph/line) and combine vector similarity search with graph-neighborhood expansion, feeding both to the LLM for more precise, explainable answers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've loaded the chunks into the graph ... we structured the chunks the document the block the paragraph the line

takeaways.technique: Shared consolidated data landscape as team accelerator
takeaways.what_they_do: Consolidating data into one graph cut the time for new engineers/data scientists to understand and clean a data landscape from ~3 months to ~3 weeks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what used to take 3 months to consolidate understand clean up took three weeks or less for for a new project

takeaways.what_they_do: Because answers come from explicit nodes and edges rather than vector probabilities, they can reason about and explain relationships and attach access controls per node.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're no longer looking at statistical probabilities in the vector space you're actually looking at graphs and nodes and edges
